title: Promoted phase transition in perovskite heterojunctions via in-situ regulated 2D intermediates enables stable solar cells - Nature Communications
byline: Yue; Shengli; Zhao; Guanghan; Zhang; Weichuan; You; Shuai; Wanfei; Yang; Rongshen; Weichao; Tinghuan; Li; Shilin; Hong; Chenglin; Zheng; Xiaopeng; Kui; Hao; Hui
html:
Abstract

The formation of 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions often relies on spacer-induced ion-exchange, which is difficult to achieve graded distribution of 2D species for efficient charge transport. Here, we report a phase-regulation strategy for formamidinium-based perovskites guided by pre-adding a full-composition 2D perovskite (hereinafter denoted as Pre-2D) into the FA-based 3D perovskite precursor. This approach enables coordinated control of precursor organization and interfacial phase evolution, resulting in bottom-up growth of phase-stable α‑FAPbI3 with vertically aligned 2D/3D heterostructures. The gradient architecture at the buried interface improves crystallographic orientation, suppresses defect-assisted recombination, and mitigates ion migration. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.61% at room temperature with a high efficiency of 28.01% at 245 K, and 23.58% for mini-modules. Notably, devices retain over 95% of initial efficiency after 1100 hours of continuous MPP tracking and 1700 hours of damp-heat testing. These findings provide a scalable route to regulate phase competition and buried-interface energetics in FA-based perovskites, advancing the development of efficient and durable perovskite photovoltaics.
